  "text": "When the library roof began leaking, Marion put buckets beneath the worst spots and moved the travel books into biography.

By closing time, Italy was sharing a shelf with Isaac Newton.

The council sent a form. Marion sent photographs. Rain was forecast for the weekend.

On Friday, a boy arrived carrying a toolbox almost as wide as his shoulders.

“My grandad says you've got a problem.”

“Your grandad is right.”

“He says you've probably written a letter about it.”

“Three.”

The boy nodded, as though this confirmed something unfortunate.

His grandfather appeared behind him, wiping his boots. Marion recognised him from the large-print section. He borrowed westerns and always returned them early.

“I'm retired,” he said. “Which means I can have a look, but you can't complain about the speed.”

They climbed into the loft. Marion stayed below, listening to footsteps pass above poetry.

An hour later, the boy came down for a bucket, two towels, and a book about moths.

“Is that for the roof?”

“No. There are some up there.”

By dusk, the dripping had stopped. His grandfather explained that the repair would hold until someone could replace the flashing properly.

“What do I owe you?” Marion asked.

He glanced towards the returns desk.

“There's a book I lost in 1987.”

Marion opened the old ledger beneath the counter.

“Title?”

“Practical Roof Repairs.”

She looked up.

He held her gaze for a moment, then smiled.

Outside, rain began again. The three of them stood listening.

Marion fetched the moth book and stamped it for the boy. Then she found the kettle, while his grandfather checked each bucket one last time."
}
